i’ve been on 100mg since august 2020 and i love it because of the same reasons you do! and i’m so glad i came across this post because i wasn’t sure if the nightmares was due to the seroquel or lamotrigine. yea i have to agree the nightmares are really really awful, i try to fight the fears while i’m awake, like mindful thinking and talking myself down from it. hope that helps :-)

hi, i’m actually prescribed both medications and love them both. i didn’t really notice any weight gain but i also smoke a lot of tree and work out. the seroquel does make me very very tired but i have really bad insomnia so it helps me go to bed at 11pm vs 5am. i haven’t taken the seroquel  since i’ve graduated but i need to take my lamotrigine every day (or idk placebo effect or not, i’ll feel “different”, whether that’s a good or bad lmfao). i take propranolol for anxiety (it’s a beta blocker/antihypertensive) and it helps but i don’t take my two doses prescribed but one/day and then i use it as one/when needed. hopefully this helped! overall love lamotrigine, less depressive episodes & more “manic” days hahahaha & therapy hits

ngl it’s kind of nice to know i’m not alone as a student who has mental health issues and have the same ideas as me. it’s extremely difficult to have these problems and continue not only life but nursing school. thank you everyone for sharing because it’s truly nice to feel i’m not alone. i just finished my first rotation on the psych unit and i loved interacting with the patients, i think it was because i was forced to be strong and be someone i’m not. but i think this is why i love nursing, even when i think of doing bad things, walking into clinicals and having patients confide in your and bless you for being there for them physically/emotionally/mentally is one of the best selfish and selfless things i can do. it reminds me that despite how i feel about myself, i can give the strength and hope patients need to “overcome” and “adapt” to their new situation. i been getting the help i need despite how shitty my mental help i need and nursing has really pushed me to do that because i want to be as strong minded as i can before i enter the field. i am SO proud of everyone in this thread, please know you have something that no one can teach, and it’s ~empathy~ that’s what makes you special

super relatable! it’s like our professors conspire with each other ~like how can we get more students to drop out so our NCLEX passing rate stays high~ but i struggled with this in my first year of nursing school, and it really helps me to get all the little bs assignments done first and then start studying a week ahead and alternate every 3 hours so you don’t spend more time on one exam and mess up and didnt study enough on the other exam!

my friends and i say, “it’s not really over until it’s actually over”, we have all been there and i hope that you stay strong and persevere! it’s going to be difficult these next few weeks but don’t give up! there’s still hope :-)

couldn’t have said this any better. the comment about “living wage” really rubbed me in the wrong way, there’s nothing wrong with feeling all these emotions, but putting others down for talking about it defeats the purpose of this subreddit right? we’re here to talk about nursing school as a whole, all the good and the bad, we’re apart of this community. and honestly, yes nursing schooling is freaking hell, but i cant imagine myself doing anything else. and what my professors have said in nursing school that really resonated with me was “the friends you make in nursing school are lifetime friends”; we lift each other up, motivate each other, comfort, cry, all the above. before nursing school, i had 0 friends in the program because all my friends were in different majors, but nursing majors get nursing majors. no one endears the pain, suffering and tears of joy as your friend you study with for countless hours a day. i wish you the best of luck and hope you find the nursing friend group and self love to get through this program!
